tabs.title: Company Overview
tabs.content:
**Marisund Logistics** is a global freight-forwarding company running a mix of Azure workloads and third-party SaaS applications used by partner customs brokers.

**Current environment:**
- An Azure Automation runbook, shared across three separate Azure subscriptions, needs to read shipment manifests from an Azure Storage account and write status updates to an Azure SQL Database in a fourth subscription.
- A partner customs-clearance SaaS application ("ClearRoute") needs to call Marisund's internal shipment API on behalf of signed-in customs brokers, using delegated permissions the brokers consent to individually.
- A separate nightly batch job (no interactive user) needs application-level access to read shipment records directly from Microsoft Graph, and this access must be approved once by an administrator rather than by each broker.

tabs.title: Workload Requirements
tabs.content:
- The Azure Automation identity used by the shared runbook must be reusable across the multiple subscriptions it touches, rather than being tied to the lifecycle of a single Azure resource.
- A legacy, on-premises customs-documentation portal (no cloud-native authentication support) must become reachable by remote customs brokers without deploying a VPN, while still enforcing Conditional Access.
- Marisund's security team wants continuous visibility into shadow IT — SaaS apps that employees are using without IT's knowledge — and the ability to apply session controls (such as blocking downloads) to sanctioned but risky apps, without requiring the apps to be reconfigured individually.
